label: Allies
summary: Allies are people within an organisation who can support and advocate for a lone conversation designer, even without holding an official role related to conversational content. They are not the same as a business sponsor or manager — they are colleagues whose day-to-day work puts them close to users, systems, or organisational power. Finding them is listed as the first practical step for a designer working alone.
how_maaike_uses: In her checklist for solo conversation designers, Maaike frames allies as a pragmatic survival strategy rather than a nice-to-have. She points to specific groups worth cultivating: customer support staff who have direct contact with the target audience, software testers and functional administrators, and secretaries or project management officers who often hold informal influence. The implication is that a lone designer's ability to do good work depends partly on building this informal network before formal authority or recognition catches up.
open_questions: How do you maintain these ally relationships over time, especially if your role or the organisation's priorities shift?
What happens when there are no natural allies available — for example in a very small or siloed organisation?
